Abstract: Discrete diffusion models have emerged as a powerful framework for generative modeling of sequential data, offering strong theoretical guarantees and competitive empirical performance. Despite their success, sampling remains computationally expensive due to the need for many iterative denoising steps. In this work, we propose an ODE-based sampler for discrete diffusion models that enables faster generation by solving a continuous-time ordinary differential equation derived from the probability flow of the discrete diffusion process. Our approach draws an analogy between continuous and discrete diffusion, adapting the probability flow ODE framework to the discrete setting. We provide theoretical justification showing that our sampler approximates the true data distribution under mild regularity conditions. Experiments on text and image generation benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves sample quality comparable to standard ancestral samplers while requiring significantly fewer function evaluations, yielding substantial speedups. Our results open the door to more efficient deployment of discrete diffusion models in practical applications.
